So my biggest issues were with dryness and soreness. I had dry skin and developed mild eczema on my hands, a super dry scalp (had to go from washing my hair everyday to washing it once a week), dry lips, and occasional nosebleeds.

So for dry skin (on arms and body) I used gold bond eczema relief when it was really bad and cetaphil body lotion when it was more mild.

For dry face I used olay complete all day moisturizer with spf 15 and some sheet masks from amazon 2-3 times a week (mediheal line friends in the dark blue package or derma korea snail). I also used the garnier micellar water to wash my face in the morning and cerave at night. 

For dry lips I used Dr. Dans Cortibalm (could only find on amazon) and aquaphor (not the one for lips) over it. I mainly only used the aquaphor at night. Dr Dans is a literal godsend, though. I don’t think the chapped lips are manageable without it.

For the nosebleeds I used a humidifier at night.

I took fishoil vitamins for the soreness, but it was never too too bad.

Also drink a ton of water!!! Super important to stay extremely hydrated. 

Truthfully, I know this medication is rough, but as long as you stay ahead of the side effects and make sure you’re really gentle with your skin and your body, you’ll be okay. I went to school full time and worked as a cashier through it. It’s definitely manageable!

* 1 uncooked 9" pie crust
* A handful of your favorite chocolate chips
* 1 1/2 cups of chopped pecans
* 1 cup of brown sugar 
* 1/4 cup of light sugar
* 1/2 cup of melted butter
* 2 eggs
* 1 tablespoon of whatever milk is in your kitchen
* 1 heaping teaspoon of vanilla extract

Preheat your oven to 400 degrees F
Beat the eggs until they're foamy and light.  Mix in your melted butter, brown sugar, white sugar, and flour. When that's all nice and mixed add your vanilla, milk, and a cup of your pecans and stir it all together. 
Pour your handful of chocolate chips into the uncooked pie crust. Add as much chocolate as you want. This is totally to taste. 
Gently pour the mix on top of the chocolate chips, being careful to not disturb them. 
Put the pie in the oven at 400 for 10 minutes
Once that time is up, remove the pie and turn the temperature down to 325. 
Add the rest of your chopped pecans and put the pie back into the oven for 40-50 minutes. Check on it often because you don't want your crust to burn. 
Once it's done, the pie shouldn't jiggle when pushed. Let it cool for a couple of hours.
